{{S}} understands the order of routines.

maths|Non-Spatial Measure.name: Days, months and calendars
maths|Non-Spatial Measure.definition: Names and orders days and months and uses a calendar.
examples: Naming and ordering the months of the year.
{{S}} uses a calendar to name the days of the week and the months of the year.

maths|Non-Spatial Measure.name: Reading and recording time
maths|Non-Spatial Measure.definition: Reads analog and digital clocks and records the time.
examples: Reading analog clocks to the half hour.
{{S}} reads analog and digital clocks to the hour, such as '12 o'clock'.

maths|Non-Spatial Measure.name: How long events take
maths|Non-Spatial Measure.definition: Uses hours, minutes and seconds and works out elapsed time.
examples: Using start and finish times to calculate the elapsed time of events.
{{S}} uses start and finish times to work out how long an event lasts.

maths|Non-Spatial Measure.name: 24-hour time and timetables
maths|Non-Spatial Measure.definition: Reads, converts and uses 24-hour time, including in timetables.
examples: Converting between 12- and 24-hour time accurately.
{{S}} converts between 12- and 24-hour time.

maths|Non-Spatial Measure.name: Money
maths|Non-Spatial Measure.definition: Counts, shows and calculates with money (bank sentences only).
examples: {{S}} calculates totals with money and compares prices.
{{S}} shows money values in different forms.

maths|Data.name: Collecting data and asking questions
maths|Data.definition: Answers, asks and chooses questions and runs surveys to gather data.
examples: Conducting a survey to collect a variety of data.
{{S}} creates surveys and records data using predicted categories.

maths|Data.name: Sorting and recording data
maths|Data.definition: Groups objects and records data with tally marks.
examples: Using tally marks to record collected data.
{{S}} groups objects by one feature and joins in class activities to make a data display.

maths|Data.name: Making graphs and displays
maths|Data.definition: Shows data with objects, pictures, tables and graphs.
examples: Creating data displays using objects or symbols.
{{S}} creates column graphs and answers questions related to the information.

maths|Data.name: Choosing a suitable graph
maths|Data.definition: Decides which type of graph or display suits the data.
examples: Recognising which type of graph is most appropriate when representing data.
{{S}} selects suitable graphs to display data.

maths|Data.name: Reading tables and graphs
maths|Data.definition: Reads and interprets information shown in tables, graphs and timelines.
examples: Interpreting information presented in picture graphs.
{{S}} interprets data from tables and column graphs.

maths|Data.name: Comparing data and drawing conclusions
maths|Data.definition: Compares categories, data sets or graphs and says what the data shows.
examples: Comparing different sets of data shown together in a column graph.
{{S}} identifies the largest and smallest values in a data display.
